explanations: There is none. The current time is injected as a function and every test pins it to an explicit UTC instant, so results do not depend on when or in which timezone the suite runs. Boundaries are tested on both sides: 600_000 vs 600_001 at noon (target 500_000 plus 10% tolerance), and 999_000 vs 999_500 for the exhausted check with a 1_000 bid. The pacer holds no mutable state, so sharing `noon` across tests is safe.

fractionOfDayElapsed is 0.5, so target is 500,000 and the ceiling adds 1,000,000 * 0.1 = 100,000, giving 600,000. The check is `spent > ceiling`, so exactly 600,000 is allowed, as the "exactly at the tolerance ceiling" test asserts. 500,000 is just the target, 550,000 has no basis in the code, and 1,000,000 ignores pacing.

The pacer computes start of day with getUTCFullYear/Month/Date. A date-time string without "Z" is parsed as local time, so on a CI machine in another timezone the UTC fraction would differ and the tests would be environment-dependent. Date parses such strings fine, the pacer has no rejection logic, and speed is unaffected.

decide() first checks spent + bid > daily: 1,000,500 > 1,000,000, so it returns exhausted before computing the pacing target. At 23:59 the ceiling is above the budget, so pacing alone would not block. There is no midnight special case.
